image_description: A low-light, high-energy concert scene featuring a band performing on an elevated stage. The stage is framed by a metal truss lighting rig overhead. Several musicians are visible, including a guitarist and vocalist. In the foreground, the backs of audience members' heads and shoulders obscure the lower portion of the view. A bright vertical flare (likely a pyrotechnic or intense light) is present on the right side of the stage.

A distinct horizontal boundary separates the lit stage area from the darker audience area, although partially occluded by people.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The hair and clothing textures of the audience members in the immediate foreground exhibit slight 'smearing' or painterly qualities typical of AI generation in complex, low-light organic patterns.
The figure on the far right has ambiguous limb definition; the arm holding the microphone/stand seems to merge slightly with the torso, and the hand structure is indistinct.
The geometry of the lighting truss shows minor inconsistencies in parallel lines, appearing slightly warped rather than perfectly rigid, though this could be attributed to lens distortion.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the scene is correctly classified as a 'stage' and not just a generic concert or party, verifying the presence of stage-specific infrastructure.
To audit the anatomical correctness of the musicians, specifically checking for extra limbs or fused fingers which are common AI artifacts in crowd/band scenes.
To verify the physical separation between the overhead rig and the stage floor, ensuring the 3D structure is logically sound and not 'melting'.
To assess the coherence of lighting sources and identify any subtle noise or blur artifacts in the low-light regions.

focus_areas: Anatomical integrity of musicians' hands and instruments
Structural rigidity of the overhead lighting truss
Boundary sharpness between stage lights and dark background
Texture consistency in the foreground audience
